subject.title: [Bug]: read tool drops memory/ prefix in multi-agent setup, causing ENOENT

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue by accepting the linked read-tool fallback for bare daily-memory filenames, or should the fix move upstream to the startup/prompt path that loses `memory/`?
rationale: Current main still has the reported failure shape, but the open fix changes read-tool fallback semantics and touches the workspace read boundary, so the final fix boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept linked fallback
options.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453 as the scoped ENOENT-only fallback while preserving sandbox validation and root-file priority.

options.title: Move upstream
options.body: Require a replacement fix in startup-context or prompt generation so the model keeps `memory/` and the generic read tool does not infer daily-memory paths.

options.title: Wait for fresh live proof
options.body: Keep the issue open without merging the fallback until a maintainer reruns the secondary-agent Windows or heartbeat path on current main.

recommendation.title: Accept linked fallback
recommendation.body: Land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96453 as the scoped ENOENT-only fallback while preserving sandbox validation and root-file priority.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining product choice is centered on the agent read-tool boundary where recent merged read-path work was concentrated.
